explanation: Awolowo founded and led the Action Group, based in the Western Region.

subject: history
text: The Northern People's Congress was led by ___.
explanation: Sir Ahmadu Bello was the Sardauna of Sokoto and leader of the NPC.

subject: history
text: Nigeria became independent on ___.
explanation: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on 1 October 1960.

subject: history
text: Nigeria became a republic in ___.
explanation: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963 with a Nigerian head of state.

subject: history
text: The first military coup in Nigeria took place in ___.
explanation: The January 1966 coup ended the First Republic.

subject: history
text: The Nigerian Civil War lasted from ___.
explanation: The civil war was fought between 1967 and 1970.

subject: history
text: The Richards Constitution of 1946 ___.
options: introduced regionalism into Nigeria's legislative structure
explanation: The Richards Constitution divided the country into three regions, strengthening regional politics.

subject: history
text: Nigeria's first President was ___.
explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first President when Nigeria became a republic in 1963.

subject: history
text: Nigeria's first Prime Minister was ___.
explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa served as Nigeria's first Prime Minister.

subject: history
text: The 1979 Constitution established a ___ system of government.
explanation: Nigeria adopted an executive presidential system in 1979.

subject: history
text: Nigeria returned to democratic rule in ___.
explanation: The Fourth Republic began on 29 May 1999.

subject: history
text: The June 12, 1993 presidential election was annulled by ___.
explanation: President Ibrahim Babangida annulled the election widely believed to have been won by MKO Abiola.

subject: history
text: The presumed winner of the June 12, 1993 election was ___.
explanation: Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola is widely regarded as the winner.

subject: history
text: The National Youth Service Corps was established in ___.
explanation: NYSC was created in 1973 to promote national unity.

subject: history
text: FESTAC '77 was a festival of ___.
options: Black and African arts and culture
explanation: The Second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture was held in Lagos in 1977.

subject: history
text: Nigeria's Fourth Republic began with the inauguration of ___ as President.
explanation: Obasanjo was sworn in on 29 May 1999.

subject: history
text: One major consequence of military rule in Nigeria was ___.
explanation: Successive military governments centralised power and suspended democratic institutions.

subject: history
text: The current Nigerian constitution was promulgated in ___.
explanation: The 1999 Constitution, as amended, is currently in force.

subject: history
text: The Nigerian oil boom of the 1970s primarily increased revenue from ___.
explanation: Oil exports became the dominant source of government revenue.

subject: history
text: The First World War lasted from ___.
explanation: World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918.

subject: history
text: The Second World War ended in ___.
explanation: World War II ended in 1945.

subject: history
text: The French Revolution began in ___.
explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille.

subject: history
text: The American Declaration of Independence was made in ___.
explanation: The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.

subject: history
text: Ancient Egyptian civilisation developed along the ___.
explanation: The Nile's annual floods supported Egyptian agriculture and settlement.

subject: history
text: The transatlantic slave trade mainly transported enslaved Africans to ___.
explanation: Millions of Africans were forcibly transported across the Atlantic to the Americas.

subject: history
text: The League of Nations was established after ___.
explanation: The League was created in 1920 as part of the post-WWI settlement.

subject: history
text: The Cold War was mainly a rivalry between the United States and ___.
explanation: The USA and USSR competed ideologically and geopolitically after 1945.

subject: history
text: The Soviet Union dissolved in ___.
explanation: The USSR formally dissolved in December 1991.

subject: history
text: Apartheid in South Africa ended with democratic elections in ___.
explanation: South Africa held its first non-racial elections in 1994, electing Nelson Mandela.

subject: history
text: The Industrial Revolution began in ___.
explanation: Britain was the first country to industrialise in the late eighteenth century.

subject: history
text: The Berlin Wall fell in ___.
explanation: The wall was opened in November 1989, symbolising the end of the Cold War division.

subject: economics
text: The fundamental economic problem is ___.
options: scarcity of resources relative to wants
explanation: Resources are limited while human wants are unlimited, creating the need to choose.

subject: economics
text: Opportunity cost is the ___.
options: value of the next best alternative forgone
explanation: Choosing one option means giving up the value of the best alternative.

subject: economics
text: According to the law of demand, as price rises, quantity demanded ___.
explanation: Price and quantity demanded are inversely related, all else equal.

subject: economics
text: The law of supply states that as price rises, quantity supplied ___.
explanation: Producers are willing to supply more at higher prices.

subject: economics
text: Equilibrium in a market occurs where ___.
explanation: Market equilibrium is where the demand and supply curves intersect.

subject: economics
text: Price elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in ___.
explanation: Price elasticity measures how much demand changes when price changes.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following is a factor of production?
explanation: The factors of production are land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.

subject: economics
text: A market with only one seller is called a ___.
explanation: A monopoly has a single seller with significant market power.

subject: economics
text: A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price will likely cause ___.
explanation: At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

subject: economics
text: Goods that are consumed together, such as bread and butter, are called ___.
explanation: Complementary goods are used jointly, so demand for one affects demand for the other.

subject: economics
text: Gross Domestic Product measures the total value of ___ produced within a country in a period.
explanation: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced domestically.

subject: economics
text: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general ___.
explanation: Inflation is a persistent increase in the general price level.

subject: economics
text: Unemployment in which workers lack skills demanded by employers is called ___.
explanation: Structural unemployment arises from a mismatch between skills and available jobs.

subject: economics
text: Fiscal policy involves the use of ___ to influence the economy.
explanation: Fiscal policy is government's use of spending and taxation.

subject: economics
text: Monetary policy is mainly carried out by the ___.
explanation: The central bank controls money supply, interest rates and credit conditions.

subject: economics
text: A recession is generally defined as a period of ___.
explanation: A recession involves a significant decline in economic activity.

subject: economics
text: A budget deficit occurs when government ___.
explanation: Deficits occur when expenditure is greater than revenue.

subject: economics
text: Aggregate demand is the total demand for ___.
options: goods and services in an economy
explanation: Aggregate demand sums consumption, investment, government spending and net exports.

subject: economics
text: The exchange rate is the price of one currency expressed in ___.
explanation: Exchange rates express the value of one currency in terms of another.

subject: economics
text: Economic growth is usually measured by the increase in ___.
explanation: Real GDP growth is the standard measure of economic growth.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following is a primary function of money?
explanation: Money serves as a medium of exchange, store of value and unit of account.

subject: economics
text: The apex bank in Nigeria is the ___.
explanation: The CBN is Nigeria's central bank and monetary authority.

subject: economics
text: Commercial banks make profit mainly by ___.
options: lending at higher interest than they pay depositors
explanation: The interest spread between lending and deposit rates generates profit.

subject: economics
text: Inflation reduces the ___ of money.
explanation: As prices rise, a given amount of money buys fewer goods and services.

subject: economics
text: M1 money supply consists mainly of ___.
options: currency in circulation and demand deposits
explanation: M1 includes currency and highly liquid demand deposits.

subject: economics
text: The process by which commercial banks create credit through lending is called ___.
explanation: Banks create deposits when they lend, expanding the money supply.

subject: economics
text: The interest rate is the ___.
explanation: Interest is the price paid for the use of borrowed money.

subject: economics
text: The Nigerian Stock Exchange facilitates the buying and selling of ___.
explanation: Stock exchanges provide a market for shares, bonds and other securities.

subject: economics
text: Insurance is a system of ___.
explanation: Pooled premiums allow insurers to compensate members for covered losses.

subject: economics
text: A development bank provides long-term finance mainly for ___.
explanation: Development banks support infrastructure, industry and long-term projects.

subject: economics
text: International trade is the exchange of goods and services between ___.
explanation: It involves cross-border exchange between countries.

subject: economics
text: The principle of comparative advantage argues that countries should specialise in goods where they have the ___.
explanation: Comparative advantage is based on lower opportunity cost of production.

subject: economics
text: The balance of trade is the difference between the value of a country's ___ and ___.
explanation: Balance of trade compares merchandise exports and imports.

subject: economics
text: A tariff is a tax imposed on ___.
explanation: Tariffs raise the price of imports and protect domestic producers.

subject: economics
text: Devaluation of a currency makes exports ___.
explanation: A weaker currency lowers export prices abroad and raises import prices at home.

subject: economics
text: ECOWAS is an organisation promoting economic integration in ___.
explanation: The Economic Community of West African States promotes regional integration.

subject: economics
text: OPEC mainly influences the price of ___.
explanation: OPEC coordinates oil production and pricing policies.

subject: economics
text: Foreign exchange reserves are held by a country to ___.
explanation: Reserves support imports, debt payments and exchange-rate stability.

subject: economics
text: A country's exports are goods and services it ___.
explanation: Exports are sold to other countries.

subject: economics
text: Imports are goods and services a country ___.
explanation: Imports are purchased from other countries.

subject: economics
text: Nigeria's major export commodity is ___.
explanation: Petroleum accounts for the largest share of Nigeria's export earnings.

subject: economics
text: Before oil became dominant, Nigeria's economy depended heavily on ___.
explanation: Agricultural exports such as cocoa, palm oil and groundnuts dominated earnings.

subject: economics
text: The currency of Nigeria is the ___.
explanation: The naira is Nigeria's legal tender.

subject: economics
text: The Central Bank of Nigeria is responsible for ___.
explanation: The CBN manages monetary policy and currency stability.

subject: economics
text: Privatisation is the transfer of state-owned enterprises to ___.
explanation: Privatisation sells public assets or management to private investors.

subject: economics
text: A subsidy is a government payment that ___.
options: lowers the cost of a good or service
explanation: Subsidies reduce production or consumption costs to support affordability.

subject: economics
text: The informal sector includes activities that are ___.
explanation: Informal enterprises operate outside formal registration and regulation.

subject: economics
text: Economic diversification means ___.
options: expanding beyond dependence on one sector
explanation: Diversification broadens the productive base beyond oil.

subject: economics
text: Nigeria's largest city by population is generally considered to be ___.
explanation: Lagos is Nigeria's largest urban agglomeration.

subject: economics
text: A major challenge of Nigeria's oil-dependent economy is ___.
explanation: Falling oil prices reduce government revenue and foreign exchange earnings.

subject: commerce
text: Trade is the exchange of goods and services for ___.
explanation: Trade involves buying and selling, often using money or barter.

subject: commerce
text: Home trade refers to trade carried out ___.
explanation: Home (domestic) trade is conducted within a country's borders.

subject: commerce
text: Foreign trade is trade between ___.
explanation: Foreign or international trade crosses national borders.

subject: commerce
text: Goods brought into a country from abroad are called ___.
explanation: Imports are purchased from other countries.

subject: commerce
text: Goods sold to other countries are called ___.
explanation: Exports are sold abroad.

subject: commerce
text: Entrepôt trade involves ___.
explanation: Entrepôt trade imports goods and re-exports them, often after processing.

subject: commerce
text: Visible trade refers to trade in ___.
explanation: Visible trade involves physical goods; invisible trade involves services.

subject: commerce
text: Invisible trade involves the exchange of ___.
explanation: Services such as shipping, banking and tourism constitute invisible trade.

subject: commerce
text: The balance of trade compares the value of a country's ___.
explanation: Balance of trade deals with merchandise (visible) imports and exports.

subject: commerce
text: The balance of payments is a record of a country's ___ with the rest of the world.
explanation: It records trade, investment and financial flows.

subject: commerce
text: A retailer sells goods ___.
explanation: Retailers sell directly to final consumers.

subject: commerce
text: A wholesaler buys in bulk and sells ___.
explanation: Wholesalers act as intermediaries between producers and retailers.

subject: commerce
text: One advantage of division of labour is ___.
explanation: Specialisation allows workers to become more efficient.

subject: commerce
text: A business owned by one person is a ___.
explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned and controlled by one individual.

subject: commerce
text: A partnership is owned by ___.
explanation: Partners contribute capital and share profits and risks.

subject: commerce
text: A company has ___ liability.
explanation: Shareholders' liability is limited to the amount they invested.

subject: commerce
text: A cooperative is owned and controlled by its ___.
explanation: Cooperatives are democratic organisations owned by members.

subject: commerce
text: A public corporation is owned by ___.
explanation: Public corporations are state-owned enterprises.

subject: commerce
text: A private limited company has the abbreviation ___.
explanation: Private limited companies use 'Ltd' in their names.

subject: commerce
text: A public limited company is quoted on the stock exchange and uses ___.
explanation: Plc companies can offer shares to the public.

subject: commerce
text: The memorandum of association states a company's ___.
explanation: It sets out the company's name, objects and capital structure.

subject: commerce
text: The articles of association contain rules governing ___.
explanation: Articles regulate internal affairs and the conduct of company business.

subject: commerce
text: A prospectus is issued to ___.
options: invite the public to subscribe for shares
explanation: A prospectus provides information to prospective investors.

subject: commerce
text: A merger occurs when two companies ___.
explanation: A merger combines two or more business entities.

subject: commerce
text: A franchise allows a person to ___ under another company's brand.
explanation: The franchisee uses the franchisor's brand and system for a fee.

subject: commerce
text: Capital is the money used to ___ a business.
explanation: Capital funds the establishment and running of a business.

subject: commerce
text: Working capital is the difference between ___.
explanation: Working capital measures short-term liquidity.

subject: commerce
text: A share represents ___ in a company.
explanation: Shareholders own a portion of the company.

subject: commerce
text: A debenture is a ___ instrument.
explanation: Debentures are long-term loans to a company, paid interest rather than dividends.

subject: commerce
text: A dividend is a share of a company's ___ paid to shareholders.
explanation: Dividends distribute profits to shareholders.

subject: commerce
text: A bank overdraft allows an account holder to ___.
options: withdraw more than the account balance within a limit
explanation: An overdraft is a short-term borrowing facility.

subject: commerce
text: Insurance protects a business against ___.
explanation: Insurance transfers specified risks to an insurer in exchange for premiums.

subject: commerce
text: A bank draft is a cheque ___.
options: drawn by a bank on itself
written by a customer without funds
explanation: A bank draft is a guaranteed payment instrument issued by a bank.

subject: commerce
text: A cheque is an order to a bank to ___.
options: pay a stated sum from the drawer's account
explanation: The drawer instructs the bank to pay the payee.

subject: commerce
text: A bill of exchange is a written order requiring the addressee to pay ___.
options: a specified sum at a stated time
explanation: It is a negotiable instrument used in trade finance.

subject: commerce
text: A budget is a plan of expected ___ and ___.
explanation: Budgets forecast revenue and spending over a period.

subject: commerce
text: Trade credit allows a buyer to ___.
options: pay for goods at a later date
sell goods on behalf of the seller
explanation: Suppliers extend credit with payment due after an agreed period.

subject: commerce
text: Which financial statement shows a business's assets, liabilities and capital at a particular date?
explanation: A balance sheet presents assets, liabilities and capital at a specific point in time.

subject: commerce
text: Marketing is best defined as ___.
options: identifying and satisfying customer needs profitably
explanation: Marketing encompasses research, product, price, promotion and distribution.

subject: commerce
text: The four Ps of marketing are product, price, place and ___.
explanation: The marketing mix comprises product, price, place and promotion.

subject: commerce
text: Market segmentation is the division of a market into ___.
explanation: Segmentation groups customers with similar needs or characteristics.

subject: commerce
text: Advertising is a paid form of ___.
explanation: Advertising communicates promotional messages through media.

subject: commerce
text: A brand is a ___ that identifies a product and distinguishes it from competitors.
explanation: Branding creates identity and customer recognition.

subject: commerce
text: Packaging helps to ___.
explanation: Packaging protects goods, provides information and supports promotion.

subject: commerce
text: A distribution channel is the route through which goods move from ___.
explanation: Channels involve intermediaries that move products to final users.

subject: commerce
text: After-sales service is important because it ___.
explanation: Support after purchase enhances satisfaction and repeat business.

subject: commerce
text: Market research is conducted to ___.
options: gather information about customers and markets
explanation: Research informs decisions about products, pricing and promotion.

subject: commerce
text: E-commerce refers to buying and selling ___.
options: over electronic networks such as the internet
explanation: E-commerce uses digital platforms to transact.

subject: commerce
text: Sales promotion includes short-term incentives such as ___.
explanation: Promotions stimulate immediate purchases through incentives.

subject: commerce
text: A market niche is a ___ segment of a market.
explanation: A niche is a narrowly defined group with specific needs.

subject: accounting
text: Accounting is best described as the process of ___.
options: identifying, recording and communicating financial information
explanation: Accounting records, classifies and communicates financial information to users.

subject: accounting
text: The going concern concept assumes that a business will ___.
options: continue operating for the foreseeable future
explanation: Financial statements are prepared on the assumption that the entity will continue in operation.

subject: accounting
text: The accrual concept recognises revenue when it is ___ and expenses when they are ___.
explanation: Accrual accounting matches revenue earned with expenses incurred, regardless of cash movement.

subject: accounting
text: The consistency concept requires a business to ___.
options: apply the same accounting methods from period to period
explanation: Consistent methods make financial statements comparable over time.

subject: accounting
text: The business entity concept treats the owner and the business as ___.
explanation: Business transactions are kept separate from the owner's personal affairs.

subject: accounting
text: Prudence in accounting means ___.
explanation: Prudence avoids overstating income or assets and understating expenses or liabilities.

subject: accounting
text: The double entry principle states that every transaction has ___.
options: two aspects: a debit and a credit
explanation: Each transaction is recorded in at least two accounts, with debits equalling credits.

subject: accounting
text: In accounting, the left side of an account is the ___ side.
explanation: Debit is conventionally the left side; credit is the right side.

subject: accounting
text: A trial balance is prepared to check the ___.
explanation: It tests whether total debits equal total credits.

subject: accounting
text: The book in which transactions are first recorded is the ___.
explanation: The journal is the book of original entry; postings go to the ledger.

subject: accounting
text: An increase in an asset is recorded as a ___.
explanation: Assets increase on the debit side.

subject: accounting
text: An increase in a liability is recorded as a ___.
explanation: Liabilities and capital increase on the credit side.

subject: accounting
text: Capital introduced by the owner is recorded as a ___.
explanation: The business owes the owner capital, so capital is credited.

subject: accounting
text: An increase in an expense is recorded as a ___.
explanation: Expenses increase on the debit side.

subject: accounting
text: Revenue earned is recorded as a ___.
explanation: Income and revenue increase on the credit side.

subject: accounting
text: Goods bought for cash are recorded as ___.
explanation: Purchases increase (debit) and cash decreases (credit).

subject: accounting
text: Goods sold for cash are recorded as ___.
explanation: Cash increases (debit) and sales income increases (credit).

subject: accounting
text: Owner's drawings are recorded as ___.
explanation: Drawings reduce capital and are debited, while cash is credited.

subject: accounting
text: A prepaid expense is treated as a ___.
explanation: Payment made in advance represents a future benefit, hence an asset.

subject: accounting
text: An accrued expense is treated as a ___.
explanation: An expense incurred but not yet paid is owed, hence a liability.

subject: accounting
text: The trading account is prepared to determine ___.
explanation: The trading account matches sales with cost of goods sold to find gross profit.

subject: accounting
text: The profit and loss account determines ___.
explanation: It deducts operating expenses and adds other income to gross profit.

subject: accounting
text: The balance sheet shows a business's ___.
explanation: It lists assets, liabilities and capital at a specific date.

subject: accounting
text: Depreciation is the ___.
options: allocation of the cost of an asset over its useful life
explanation: Depreciation spreads an asset's cost over its expected useful life.

subject: accounting
text: Closing stock is classified as a ___.
explanation: Unsold goods at year end are a current asset.

subject: accounting
text: Cost of goods sold is calculated as ___.
explanation: COGS = opening stock + purchases − closing stock.

subject: accounting
text: If sales are ₦100,000 and cost of goods sold is ₦60,000, gross profit is ___.
explanation: Gross profit = sales − cost of goods sold = 100,000 − 60,000 = ₦40,000.

subject: accounting
text: If gross profit is ₦40,000 and expenses are ₦15,000, net profit is ___.
explanation: Net profit = gross profit − expenses = 40,000 − 15,000 = ₦25,000.

subject: accounting
text: The accounting equation is ___.
explanation: Resources (assets) are financed by owners' capital and liabilities.

subject: accounting
text: A bad debt is a debt that ___.
explanation: Bad debts are receivables that have become irrecoverable and are written off.

subject: accounting
text: The current ratio is calculated as ___.
explanation: It measures short-term liquidity.

subject: accounting
text: The acid test ratio excludes ___ from current assets.
explanation: The quick ratio removes inventory, the least liquid current asset.

subject: accounting
text: Gross profit margin is ___.
explanation: It expresses gross profit as a percentage of sales.

subject: accounting
text: Net profit margin is ___.
explanation: It shows how much of each naira of sales remains as net profit.

subject: accounting
text: Return on capital employed is ___.
explanation: It measures the profit generated relative to capital invested.

subject: accounting
text: Stock turnover is calculated as ___.
options: cost of goods sold ÷ average stock
average stock ÷ cost of goods sold
explanation: It indicates how many times stock is sold and replaced in a period.

subject: accounting
text: The debtors' collection period measures the average time taken to ___.
explanation: It estimates how long receivables remain outstanding.

subject: accounting
text: Gearing measures the proportion of a company's capital that is ___.
explanation: Gearing compares debt to total capital employed.

subject: accounting
text: Earnings per share is calculated as ___.
options: profit after tax ÷ number of ordinary shares
explanation: EPS shows profit attributable to each ordinary share.

subject: accounting
text: Working capital equals ___.
explanation: It measures funds available for day-to-day operations.

subject: accounting
text: Cost accounting is mainly concerned with ___.
options: recording and controlling costs of production
explanation: It gathers cost information for planning, control and decision-making.

subject: accounting
text: Prime cost consists of ___.
options: direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses
explanation: Prime cost is the sum of direct production costs.

subject: accounting
text: Direct materials are materials that ___.
options: become part of the finished product
cannot be traced to a product
explanation: Direct materials can be identified with a specific product.

subject: accounting
text: Factory overhead includes ___.
explanation: Overheads are indirect costs such as factory rent and supervision.

subject: accounting
text: A fixed cost is one that ___.
options: does not change with output in the short run
explanation: Fixed costs, like rent, remain constant over a relevant output range.

subject: accounting
text: A variable cost is one that ___.
options: varies directly with the level of output
explanation: Variable costs change in proportion to activity.

subject: accounting
text: Break-even point occurs where ___.
explanation: At break-even, there is neither profit nor loss.

subject: accounting
text: If fixed costs are ₦100,000 and contribution per unit is ₦20, the break-even quantity is ___ units.
explanation: Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit = 100,000 ÷ 20 = 5,000.

subject: accounting
text: Marginal costing focuses on ___ costs.
explanation: Marginal costing separates variable costs from fixed costs.

subject: accounting
text: Standard costing compares actual costs with ___.
explanation: Variances between actual and standard costs guide control.

subject: geography
text: The Earth is the ___ planet from the Sun.
explanation: Mercury, Venus and Earth make Earth the third planet from the Sun.

subject: geography
text: The rotation of the Earth on its axis causes ___.
explanation: One complete rotation takes about 24 hours, producing day and night.

subject: geography
text: The revolution of the Earth around the Sun causes ___.
explanation: The tilt of the Earth's axis combined with revolution produces seasonal changes.

subject: geography
text: The Equator is a line of ___ at 0°.
explanation: The Equator is the zero-degree line of latitude.

subject: geography
text: The Prime Meridian passes through ___.
explanation: The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through Greenwich, London.

subject: geography
text: The layer of the atmosphere where weather occurs is the ___.
explanation: Most weather phenomena occur in the troposphere.

subject: geography
text: Weather differs from climate because weather refers to ___.
explanation: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place.

subject: geography
text: The process by which wind and water wear away rock and soil is called ___.
explanation: Erosion transports weathered material away.

subject: geography
text: The theory of plate tectonics explains the movement of the Earth's ___.
explanation: Plates move on the asthenosphere, causing earthquakes and mountain building.

subject: geography
text: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust through which ___ erupts.
explanation: Magma, gases and ash escape through volcanic vents.

subject: geography
text: The water cycle involves evaporation, condensation and ___.
explanation: Water moves through evaporation, condensation, precipitation and runoff.

subject: geography
text: The uppermost layer of the Earth's surface in which plants grow is called ___.
explanation: Soil supports plant growth and is formed from weathered rock and organic matter.

subject: geography
text: A delta is formed where a river ___.
explanation: Deposition at a river mouth builds a delta.

subject: geography
text: A census is the official counting of a country's ___.
explanation: A census collects demographic data about the population.

subject: geography
text: Migration is the movement of people from ___.
options: one job to another in the same office
explanation: Migration involves a change of permanent residence.

subject: geography
text: Urbanisation is the increasing proportion of a population living in ___.
explanation: Urbanisation reflects growth in urban population and settlement.

subject: geography
text: Farming is an example of a ___ activity.
explanation: Primary activities extract resources directly from nature.

subject: geography
text: Manufacturing is a ___ activity.
explanation: Secondary activities process raw materials into finished goods.

subject: geography
text: Banking and teaching are examples of ___ activities.
explanation: Tertiary activities provide services.

subject: geography
text: A push factor in migration is something that ___.
options: encourages people to leave an area
explanation: Push factors include unemployment, conflict and poor services.

subject: geography
text: The birth rate is the number of births per ___ people per year.
explanation: Birth rate is usually expressed per 1,000 population per year.

subject: geography
text: The dependency ratio compares dependants with the ___ population.
explanation: It relates children and elderly dependants to the working-age population.

subject: geography
text: A settlement is a place where people ___.
explanation: Settlements range from hamlets to megacities.

subject: geography
text: An industry located near raw materials is said to be ___.
explanation: Weight-losing industries often locate near their raw materials.

subject: geography
text: Transportation is important because it ___.
explanation: Transport facilitates movement of people, goods and services.

subject: geography
text: A megacity is an urban area with a population of more than ___ million people.
explanation: A megacity is commonly defined as having over 10 million inhabitants.

subject: geography
text: Map scale is the ratio between distance on a map and ___.
explanation: Scale allows map distances to be converted to real distances.

subject: geography
text: Contour lines join points of equal ___.
explanation: Contours represent relief on a topographic map.

subject: geography
text: A bearing is measured clockwise from ___.
explanation: Bearings are measured in degrees clockwise from north.

subject: geography
text: A map scale of 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map represents ___.
explanation: 1 cm represents 50,000 cm, which is 500 m.

subject: geography
text: On a map, closely spaced contour lines indicate ___.
explanation: Close contours indicate a rapid change in elevation.

subject: geography
text: If the local time at 0° longitude is 12:00, the local time at 15°E is approximately ___.
explanation: Every 15° of longitude corresponds to one hour; 15°E is one hour ahead of 0°.

subject: geography
text: The distance between two points on a map is measured with a ___.
explanation: Map distances are measured and then converted using the scale.

subject: geography
text: Relief on a map refers to the ___.
options: shape and height of the land
explanation: Relief describes differences in elevation and landform.

subject: geography
text: A cross-section drawn from a map shows the ___.
options: profile of the land along a line
explanation: A cross-section shows changes in height along a transect.

subject: geography
text: GPS stands for ___.
explanation: GPS uses satellites to determine location.

subject: geography
text: Altitude is the height of a place above ___.
explanation: Altitude is vertical height referenced to mean sea level.

subject: geography
text: Drainage on a map is shown by ___.
explanation: Drainage features include rivers, streams and lakes.

subject: geography
text: The capital city of Nigeria is ___.
explanation: Abuja became the federal capital in 1991.

subject: geography
text: Nigeria's largest river is the ___.
explanation: The Niger is Nigeria's principal river and gave the country its name.

subject: geography
text: The Niger and Benue rivers meet at ___.
explanation: The confluence of the Niger and Benue is at Lokoja.

subject: geography
text: Nigeria's highest mountain is ___.
explanation: Chappal Waddi in Taraba State is Nigeria's highest point.

subject: geography
text: Lake Chad lies mainly in the ___ of Nigeria.
explanation: Lake Chad borders Borno and other Sahelian states.

subject: geography
text: The tropical rainforest belt in Nigeria is found mainly in the ___.
explanation: High rainfall supports rainforest in southern Nigeria.

subject: geography
text: The Sahel savanna is characterised by ___.
explanation: The Sahel is a semi-arid transition zone south of the Sahara.

subject: geography
text: Nigeria's largest city by population is ___.
explanation: Lagos is Nigeria's largest metropolitan area.

subject: geography
text: Most of Nigeria's crude oil is produced in the ___.
explanation: The Niger Delta region is the centre of petroleum production.

subject: geography
text: The Harmattan is a ___ wind.
explanation: The Harmattan blows from the Sahara during the dry season.

subject: geography
text: Nigeria has ___ states plus the Federal Capital Territory.
explanation: There are 36 states and the FCT.

subject: geography
text: The Zuma Rock is located in ___.
explanation: Zuma Rock is a prominent monolith near Madalla in Niger State.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Photosynthesis in green plants produces glucose and ___.
explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water with light energy to produce glucose and oxygen.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Seed germination requires water, oxygen and ___.
explanation: Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature trigger germination.

subject: agricultural-science
text: NPK fertiliser supplies nitrogen, phosphorus and ___.
explanation: NPK stands for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Crop rotation helps to ___.
options: maintain soil fertility and reduce pests
explanation: Rotating crops replenishes nutrients and breaks pest cycles.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A weed is a plant that ___.
options: grows where it is not wanted
explanation: Weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients and light.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A major insect pest of stored grains is the ___.
explanation: Weevils damage stored maize, beans and other grains.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Irrigation is the artificial application of ___ to crops.
explanation: Irrigation supplies water where rainfall is insufficient.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Harvesting is the process of ___ crops.
explanation: Mature crops are gathered at harvest.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Cassava is mainly grown for its ___.
explanation: Cassava roots are processed into garri, fufu and flour.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Maize is a ___ crop.
explanation: Maize is a cereal grain.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Cocoa is a major cash crop in Nigeria and is used to produce ___.
explanation: Cocoa beans are processed into chocolate and cocoa products.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Rice grows best in ___.
explanation: Rice thrives in flooded or well-irrigated paddies.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A disease of crops caused by fungi is ___.
explanation: Blight is a fungal disease affecting many crops.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A ruminant animal has a ___ stomach.
explanation: Ruminants such as cattle and goats have four stomach chambers.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Poultry farming involves raising ___.
explanation: Poultry includes chickens, turkeys, ducks and guinea fowl.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Cattle are kept mainly for ___.
explanation: Cattle provide milk, meat, hides and draught power.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Fish farming is also known as ___.
explanation: Aquaculture is the controlled rearing of aquatic organisms.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Animal feed is called ___ when it provides all required nutrients.
explanation: A balanced ration supplies energy, protein, vitamins and minerals in correct proportions.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Vaccination protects animals against ___.
explanation: Vaccines stimulate immunity against specific pathogens.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Goats are kept for milk, meat and ___.
explanation: Goat skins are used in leather production.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Pigs are mainly raised for ___.
explanation: Pig production supplies pork.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Beekeeping is known as ___.
explanation: Apiculture is the keeping of bees for honey and wax.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Foot-and-mouth disease affects ___.
explanation: It is a highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed livestock.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Animal breeding aims to ___.
explanation: Selective breeding improves productivity, health and quality.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Which of these is an animal product?
explanation: Milk is produced by animals such as cattle and goats.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Pasture is land covered with ___ used for grazing.
explanation: Improved pasture provides nutritious forage for livestock.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Soil is formed through the breakdown of ___ over time.
explanation: Weathering of rocks and decay of organic matter produce soil.

subject: agricultural-science
text: The best soil for most crops is ___ soil.
explanation: Loam balances sand, silt and clay, retaining water and nutrients while draining well.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Soil pH measures soil ___.
explanation: pH indicates whether soil is acidic, neutral or alkaline.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Which practice helps control soil erosion?
explanation: Contour ploughing slows runoff and reduces erosion.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Humus is ___.
explanation: Humus improves soil structure, water retention and fertility.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A soil profile is a vertical section showing soil ___.
explanation: Soil horizons are distinct layers visible in a profile.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Which is an organic fertiliser?
explanation: Manure is organic matter; the others are inorganic fertilisers.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Farmyard manure improves soil by adding ___.
explanation: Manure adds nutrients and improves soil structure.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Waterlogging can be reduced by ___.
explanation: Drainage channels remove excess water from the soil.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Soil texture refers to the relative proportions of ___.
explanation: Texture depends on particle size composition.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Tillage is the preparation of soil by ___.
explanation: Tillage loosens and prepares soil for planting.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Soil conservation aims to ___.
options: prevent loss of soil fertility and erosion
explanation: Conservation practices protect soil from degradation.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Farm records are kept to ___.
explanation: Records track costs, yields and profits for informed management.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A farm budget is a plan of expected ___ and ___.
explanation: Budgets forecast farm revenue and costs.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A cooperative society helps farmers by ___.
explanation: Cooperatives provide credit, inputs and marketing support.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Agricultural extension workers help farmers by ___.
explanation: Extension services link research to farmers.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Mechanisation in agriculture means using ___ to do farm work.
explanation: Mechanisation replaces or supplements labour with machinery.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Agricultural marketing involves ___.
options: moving produce from farm to consumers at a profit
explanation: Marketing includes storage, transport, grading and selling.

subject: agricultural-science
text: A major source of farm finance is ___.
explanation: Farmers obtain credit from banks, cooperatives and government schemes.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Labour is a ___ of production.
explanation: Labour is one of the factors of production, alongside land, capital and entrepreneurship.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Land tenure refers to the system of ___ land.
explanation: Land tenure defines ownership, access and use rights.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Farm risks include ___.
explanation: Agriculture faces biological, climatic and market risks.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Agroforestry combines trees with ___.
explanation: Agroforestry integrates trees into farming systems for multiple benefits.

subject: agricultural-science
text: Sustainable agriculture aims to ___.
options: meet present needs without harming future productivity
explanation: Sustainability balances productivity, profitability and environmental care.

subject: civic-education
text: Human rights are rights that belong to every person by virtue of being ___.
explanation: Human rights are inherent, universal and inalienable.

subject: civic-education
text: The right to life is protected by the ___.
explanation: Fundamental rights, including the right to life, are guaranteed in the constitution.

subject: civic-education
text: Freedom of expression allows citizens to ___.
explanation: Free expression is protected within legal limits.

subject: civic-education
text: The right to fair hearing means a person accused of a crime is entitled to ___.
explanation: Fair hearing includes the right to defend oneself before an impartial court.

subject: civic-education
text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in ___.
explanation: The UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948.

subject: civic-education
text: Which of the following is a civic duty of a citizen?
explanation: Citizens are expected to pay lawful taxes.

subject: civic-education
text: The right to freedom of movement allows a citizen to ___.
options: move freely within the country subject to law
explanation: Movement rights are guaranteed but subject to lawful restrictions.

subject: civic-education
text: Children have the right to ___.
explanation: The Child Rights Act protects children's welfare and education.

subject: civic-education
text: Voting in elections is both a right and a ___.
explanation: Citizens should participate responsibly in choosing leaders.

subject: civic-education
text: Public property should be ___.
explanation: Caring for public property is a civic responsibility.

subject: civic-education
text: The National Human Rights Commission in Nigeria is responsible for ___.
explanation: The NHRC investigates rights abuses and promotes awareness.

subject: civic-education
text: Rights are not absolute because ___.
options: their exercise must not infringe on others' rights
explanation: Rights are balanced against public safety and the rights of others.

subject: civic-education
text: A major duty of a citizen towards the state is ___.
explanation: Lawful obedience is fundamental to orderly society.

subject: civic-education
text: Democracy is best defined as government by ___.
explanation: Democracy derives its authority from the consent of the governed.

subject: civic-education
text: A key feature of democracy is ___.
explanation: Regular competitive elections are central to democracy.

subject: civic-education
text: The principle of majority rule must be balanced with ___.
explanation: Democracies protect minorities from the tyranny of the majority.

subject: civic-education
text: A political opposition is important in a democracy because it ___.
explanation: Opposition parties scrutinise government and offer alternatives.

subject: civic-education
text: A constitution performs the function of ___.
explanation: Constitutions establish institutions and limits on power.

subject: civic-education
text: Separation of powers divides government into ___.
explanation: The three branches check and balance one another.

subject: civic-education
text: Suffrage is the right to ___.
explanation: Suffrage is the right to vote in elections.

subject: civic-education
text: Political participation includes all of the following EXCEPT ___.
explanation: Democracy depends on participation; permanently rejecting civic duties undermines it.

subject: civic-education
text: Civil society organisations contribute to democracy by ___.
options: advocating public interests and monitoring power
explanation: CSOs promote accountability, rights and civic engagement.

subject: civic-education
text: A free press is important in a democracy because it ___.
explanation: Independent media support informed public debate.

subject: civic-education
text: A referendum is a direct vote by citizens on a ___ issue.
explanation: Referendums allow voters to decide a particular question directly.

subject: civic-education
text: Accountability in a democracy means that public officials ___.
options: must answer for their actions and use of power
explanation: Accountability ensures power is exercised responsibly.

subject: civic-education
text: A democratic election should be conducted by ___.
explanation: An impartial electoral commission builds public trust in results.

subject: civic-education
text: The rule of law means that ___.
options: everyone is subject to the law
explanation: No one, including government officials, is above the law.

subject: civic-education
text: Equality before the law means that ___.
options: all persons are subject to the same legal standards
explanation: The law applies equally regardless of status or wealth.

subject: civic-education
text: Due process requires that a person cannot be punished without ___.
explanation: Due process protects individuals from arbitrary state action.

subject: civic-education
text: An independent judiciary is essential because courts must ___.
explanation: Judicial independence safeguards fairness and rights.

subject: civic-education
text: Habeas corpus protects a person against ___.
explanation: Habeas corpus requires authorities to justify detention before a court.

subject: civic-education
text: The presumption of innocence means an accused person is ___.
explanation: The burden of proof lies on the prosecution.

subject: civic-education
text: The right to appeal allows a convicted person to ___.
options: ask a higher court to review the decision
explanation: Appeals provide a check against judicial error.

subject: civic-education
text: Constitutional supremacy means that any law inconsistent with the constitution is ___.
options: void to the extent of the inconsistency
explanation: The constitution is the supreme law; inconsistent provisions are invalid.

subject: civic-education
text: Legal aid provides ___ to those who cannot afford it.
explanation: Legal aid promotes access to justice for indigent citizens.

subject: civic-education
text: A fair trial includes ___.
options: an impartial court and the right to defend oneself
explanation: Fair procedures are essential to justice.

subject: civic-education
text: Arbitrary arrest is a violation of ___.
explanation: Arrests must have legal basis and follow due process.

subject: civic-education
text: The law should be applied ___.
options: according to the wealth of parties
explanation: Consistent, impartial application is central to the rule of law.

subject: civic-education
text: Integrity means ___.
options: being honest and having strong moral principles
explanation: Integrity is consistency between values, words and actions.

subject: civic-education
text: Honesty is important because it ___.
explanation: Honesty underpins trust in personal and public life.

subject: civic-education
text: Discipline involves ___.
options: self-control and obedience to lawful rules
explanation: Discipline supports order, responsibility and achievement.

subject: civic-education
text: Patriotism is love and loyalty towards one's ___.
explanation: Patriots show commitment to their nation's wellbeing.

subject: civic-education
text: Nationalism in Nigeria can be promoted by ___.
options: respecting national symbols and contributing to development
explanation: Shared commitment to the nation strengthens unity.

subject: civic-education
text: National unity in Nigeria is best promoted by ___.
options: tolerance and equal treatment of all groups
explanation: Fairness and tolerance build cohesion in a diverse society.

subject: civic-education
text: Tolerance means ___.
explanation: Tolerance respects diversity while maintaining lawful boundaries.

subject: civic-education
text: Hard work is a national value because it ___.
explanation: Diligence drives personal and national development.

subject: civic-education
text: Self-reliance means ___.
options: using one's own efforts and resources
explanation: Self-reliance emphasises initiative and responsible independence.

subject: civic-education
text: Corruption is harmful because it ___.
explanation: Corruption diverts resources and weakens public institutions.

subject: civic-education
text: Nigerian national symbols include the flag, anthem and ___.
explanation: The coat of arms is an official national symbol.

subject: civic-education
text: Good citizenship requires a balance between rights and ___.
explanation: Rights carry corresponding duties and responsibilities.
